name: Lewis Powell

summary.text: Lewis F. Powell, Jr., a Richmond corporate lawyer later appointed to the U.S. Supreme Court, wrote the memorandum 'Attack on American Free Enterprise System' on August 23, 1971, addressed to Eugene B. Sydnor, Jr., chair of the Education Committee of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, less than two months before his Supreme Court nomination. The memo set out how business should defend against what it called a broad attack on the economic system, and became public after columnist Jack Anderson reported on it in 1972. The typescript is held in the Powell Archives at Washington and Lee University School of Law.

openQuestions: The site says the memo urged the Chamber to fund a campaign to shape universities, the media, the courts and politics, and that think tanks and legal groups followed. The archive description supports the first part in general terms; the causal claim about later organisations is historians' interpretation and is not recorded as a fact here.
